title: fix(app-shell): retire DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL, so no server upgrade URL means no upgrade CTA
body:
Fixes #10437
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL` (`'/settings/billing'`) is deleted from `packages/app-shell/src/environment/entitlements.ts`, along with all five places that read it. The control plane names the upgrade destination:

- `entitlementDialogFromError` (the 403 path): when `error.details.upgrade_url` is present, the "Upgrade plan" CTA links to it verbatim. When it is absent or empty, the spec carries no `cta`, and the dialog still explains the gate. The same function already handled `contact_url` this way.
- `upgradeDialogSpec` (the proactive prompt): when `state.upgradeUrl` is present, the prompt gets a CTA. When it is absent, the prompt has no `cta`.
- `useEnvironmentEntitlements`: the summary's `upgradeUrl` passes through verbatim, like its sibling `contactSalesUrl`. The row-derived and unknown states carry no URL. `EnvironmentEntitlementsState.upgradeUrl` becomes optional.
- `EnvironmentEntitlementDialog`: no code change. It already renders the CTA only when `spec.cta` exists. Its header comment cited `/settings/billing` as a URL that "always lands on the real page". That sentence now states the rule: no URL, no CTA.

This follows objectui#7273, which removed the tenant Console's hard-coded upgrade fallback so that "no upstream value ⇒ no link at all" (the `onUpgrade` guard in `AiChatPage` and the AI usage ring's `showCta`). The PR introduces no new pattern and no new i18n keys. `DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL` was not re-exported from the package entry, so the published `exports` surface does not move. Tree-wide `git grep DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL` now returns 0 hits (control: `decideEnvironmentCta` hits in 3 files).

## Why the path was dead

The CTA is a full-page anchor resolved against `apiBase`, the control-plane origin. The Console declares `settings` only as a child route of `/organizations/:slug` (the `DefaultSettingsPage` route in `apps/console/src/App.tsx`). The control plane mounts its console under `/_console`. No router serves `/settings/billing`.

## Triage guard: what the control plane sends (measured, with a reading gap)

Triage asked for a check of what cloud supplies before the fallback is removed. These sources could be read:

- **`objectstack-ai/cloud` is unreadable from this session.** `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/cloud/issues/1869` answers 403: "GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session". The emitter of `upgrade_url` / `upgradeUrl` on the entitlement surfaces could not be read at its source. **This is a declared reading gap.**
- **`@objectstack/spec` declares neither key anywhere.** objectstack `origin/main` `fa00ebf` `packages/spec` has 0 hits (control: `ApiErrorSchema` hits in the same tree). `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` also has 0 hits; that is npm `latest` and the version this repo installs (control: `ApiErrorSchema` hits in its `dist`). The entitlement wire shape is owned by cloud, and there is no spec declaration to align to.
- **objectstack's `RuntimeConfigPlugin` (`packages/cloud-connection`) states the same contract.** For its adjacent `upgradeUrl` key on `GET /api/v1/runtime/config`, it says the key is absent by default and that "the Console reads 'no key' as 'no link'". It also names a relative path such as `/settings/billing` as "the control plane's own current `upgrade_url` dialect". That is second-hand evidence that the cloud emitter currently sends a value on the 403 path.
- **This repo's own fixtures assume the server sends the URL.** `useConsoleActionRuntime.test.tsx` models the 403 as `details: { upgrade_url: '/settings/billing', plan: 'free' }`.

This does not swap a tolerant default for a hard failure. When the server omits the URL, the dialog still opens with its title and body, and only the link is withheld. Before this change, that link was a full-page navigation to a path no router serves. When the server does send a URL, behaviour is unchanged; the control pins below prove this on the base.

**Triage's p2 question is NOT MEASURED.** Whether real hosts hit the default (a cloud summary or 403 without a URL) is a fact about the cloud emitter, which cannot be read here. One structural reading does hold. The row-derived and unknown states never reach the upgrade prompt: `decideEnvironmentCta` returns `upgrade_for_development` only when `canCreateDevelopmentEnv === false`, and only the summary sets that. So the hook's three reads of the default were dead for the dialog. The default could reach a user only through a summary or a 403 that carried no URL.

## Tests: red on the base, green on the head

New pins, all in `packages/app-shell/src/environment/__tests__/`:

- `entitlements.test.ts`, block `no server upgrade_url ⇒ no upgrade CTA (objectui#10437)`: covers DEV_ENV_PLAN_LOCKED and DEV_ENV_LIMIT without a URL, and an empty-string URL. The control is a server URL becoming the CTA verbatim. Under `upgradeDialogSpec`: one pin withholds the CTA with no `upgradeUrl`, one control passes a summary URL through, and one parity pin checks the no-URL case.
- `useEnvironmentEntitlements.test.tsx`, block `no synthesized upgrade URL (objectui#10437)`: a summary without a URL, the derived state and the unknown state each carry no URL. The derived and unknown pins assert that the key is ABSENT. The control is a summary URL passing through verbatim.
- `EnvironmentEntitlementDialog.test.tsx`, block `no server URL, no upgrade CTA (objectui#10437)`: this block goes through the real builders into the real dialog. A 403 without a URL renders no anchor, and neither does the proactive prompt from a state without a URL. The control is a server URL rendering an anchor to exactly that URL.

The control pins use a server URL that deliberately differs from the retired default, so a CTA that carries it can only have come from the server.

**Red leg.** The implementation was committed first. Then the three implementation files were checked out at base `660d31185`, and the on-disk blob hashes were confirmed equal to base (`DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL` counted 3 times in `entitlements.ts`). The new tests were kept. The run was under a `trap` restore. `vitest run` of the three test files gave `Test Files 3 failed (3)`, `Tests 11 failed | 34 passed (45)`. The 11 failures are exactly the no-URL pins, and each failed on the retired default:

- `expected { label: 'Upgrade plan', …(1) } to be undefined`, where the received value carries `"url": "/settings/billing"`
- the anchor `href="/settings/billing"`, which was expected to be null
- the hook's `'/settings/billing'`, which was expected to be undefined, or its `upgradeUrl` key being present

The controls passed on the base. Restore was `git checkout HEAD -- …`. After it, `git diff HEAD` was empty and all three blob hashes equalled HEAD's.

**Green.** `vitest run packages/app-shell/src/environment/ packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useConsoleActionRuntime.test.tsx` gave `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 117 passed (117)`.

**Fixture triage.**

- `entitlements.test.ts`: two strictness pins proved that a sibling key is ignored by asserting `cta.url === DEFAULT_UPGRADE_URL`. They now assert that `cta` is undefined. That is stronger: reading a sibling `upgrade_url` would now produce a CTA and turn them red. The old pin "falls back to a default upgrade_url when the server omits one" is replaced by the no-URL block. The localization pin asserts the CTA label, so it now sends a server `upgrade_url`.
- `EnvironmentListToolbar.test.tsx`: its `UNRESOLVED` fixture mirrors the hook's unknown state, which no longer carries a URL, so the fixture's `upgradeUrl` is dropped. This file is next to the claimed ones and is declared here: one line changed, no assertion changed.
- Other fixtures that pass `upgradeUrl: '/settings/billing'` model a server-supplied value and still do.

## Gates, all at head `6bbeebfc4`

- **App-shell tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/` gave `Test Files 1 failed | 783 passed | 1 skipped (785)`, `Tests 1 failed | 7748 passed | 9 skipped (7758)`. The one failure is outside this diff; see Acceptance notes.
- **Type check.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exited 0, and the script name `type-check` was echoed. It ran after the dependency closure was built with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (exit 0). A `--listFiles` run of `tsconfig.test.json` lists all six `environment/__tests__` files.
- **Changeset presence.** `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exited 0. It found 7 source files of 1 released package changed and 1 changeset declared: `.changeset/10437-retire-default-upgrade-url.md` (`'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`).
- **Line citations.** `pnpm check:new-line-citations` printed `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)` and exited 0.
- **Control bytes.** `pnpm check:control-bytes` printed OK and exited 0.
- **Other lock-free gates, each exit 0:** `pnpm changeset:check`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:phantom-deps`, `node scripts/check-vi-mock-override-shape.mjs` and `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --changed`.
- **Doc and README gates.** None were run, because the diff touches no `.md` or docs file other than the changeset, and no export.

**Lint, narrowed to the 7 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files and declared.** The narrowing rests on three pieces of evidence:

1. The population comes from eslint itself: `eslint --print-config` resolves 116 to 119 rules for each file, so all 7 are in scope and none is ignored.
2. `--format json` reports 7 files, 0 errors and 15 warnings. Every warning is on a line this diff does not add (`no-explicit-any`, `set-state-in-effect`, `only-export-components`). The added lines contain no `any` and no `setState`.
3. Type-aware linting is not enabled: `parserOptions.project` and `projectService` are absent in every file's resolved config, and no `eslint-rules/` rule reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **An unrelated test failed once in the full app-shell run.** `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.inaccessibleAppStrand.test.tsx`, test "bounces to the DECLARED landing where the deployment declares one (objectui#7373)", was stopped by the network-escape guard: it reached a real socket at `http://localhost:3000/api/v1/meta` (plus `/meta/package` and `/meta/diagnostics`). The same file rerun alone at the same head gave `Tests 6 passed (6)`. This diff does not touch that file or any metadata fetch path. It is recorded in the report as a candidate finding; the seat decides whether to file it.
- **The cloud half is independent and is not addressed here.** objectstack-ai/cloud#1869 (the emitter's `UPGRADE_URL` literal) remains open; the card declares the two halves land in either order.
